usage.notes: Use RxNorm as Panacea's U.S. medication identity/normalization source through the canonical server adapter. The adapter supports exact name->RxCUI resolution, related SCD/SBD concepts, and approximate-term->canonical-name normalization for orchestration fallbacks. The online NLM APIs are free but limited to 20 requests/second/IP; NLM recommends caching responses for 12-24 hours.

license.identifier: NLM non-proprietary RxNorm content; API Terms of Service
license.scope: NLM states that RxNorm API and Prescribable RxNorm content are non-proprietary and, with one exception, no license is needed. The proprietary-information function can expose restricted source-vocabulary content and requires a valid UMLS license/API authorization for those sources. RxClass can include separately licensed SNOMED CT content and is outside the unrestricted RxNorm-only scope.
license.notes: Include the NLM-requested attribution/disclaimer in Panacea documentation or acknowledgements. Do not use NLM name/logo as product endorsement. Keep unrestricted RXNORM content separate from proprietary UMLS/SNOMED/source-vocabulary data.

validation.notes: RxNorm normalizes medication identity and relationships; an exact or approximate RXCUI/canonical-name match does not validate dose, indication, contraindication, interaction, prescribing appropriateness or patient-specific treatment. RxNav drug-drug interaction features were discontinued on January 2, 2024, so Panacea must not present RxNorm/RxNav as a current DDI engine.

provenance.notes: Persist RXCUI, canonical RxNorm name, concept status, term type (TTY) where used, source vocabulary when relevant, and the RxNorm release/API version observed during normalization. Preserve the original medication string so users can audit exact or approximate normalization from source text to RxNorm concept.

adapter.notes: Canonical production adapter sanitizes/bounds medication text, resolves exact names to numeric RXCUI for SCD/SBD related concepts, and separately supports approximateTerm->numeric RXCUI->RxNorm Name canonical normalization. It rejects malformed upstream identifiers, applies timeouts and does not perform drug-drug interaction checking or prescribing recommendations. Higher-level drugInfo orchestration reuses this normalization path rather than issuing duplicate RxNav requests.

trust.notes: High authority for U.S. medication terminology/normalization. License clarity is reduced because proprietary UMLS source vocabularies and RxClass/SNOMED have separate conditions outside unrestricted RxNorm content.
